papers.title: Ramanujan Challenge Results: AI-Assisted Evaluation Pipeline for Multi-Format Proofs
papers.abstract: As AI's mathematical capabilities rapidly improve, meaningful benchmarks are shifting from university-level problems and math olympiads to research-level mathematics. The Ramanujan Challenge is a benchmark comprised of research-level problems in number theory, including unpublished results and open conjectures. It presented concrete formulas for mathematical constants whose correctness can be checked numerically, while their proofs may require non-obvious mathematics. Here, we analyze the Challenge submissions, measuring the relative success of different AI models, Computer Algebra Systems (CAS), and formal tools. We find correct submissions that are conceptually distinct from the official solutions, and a proof of one of the published open conjectures. Evaluating the submissions exposed a second challenge: judging complex proofs reliably at scale. We introduce an AI-assisted evaluation pipeline for natural language proofs, CAS code, and Lean formalizations that assesses semantic and logical correctness. Compared with the conventional one-shot LLM judgment, our pipeline reduces false-positive verdicts on natural language proofs from 23% to 6% and improves judgment accuracy on supporting code from 46% to 58%. This approach provides a methodology for evaluating research-level mathematics at scale, with potential applications across mathematics and AI for science.

papers.title: The 120-Cell Dissected by the Hyperplanes of Its Final Stellation: the golden ring Z[phi] as foundation, from Kramer's seven cells to 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits
papers.abstract: The diagonals of a regular pentagon dissect it into eleven pieces and draw a pentagram; the dodecahedron dissected by the twelve face planes of its inner core gives Kramer's seven "elementary cells" of 1982. We define the stellation dissection of a golden regular polytope in any dimension as the dissection of the convex hull of its final regular stellation by the facet hyperplanes of the core, show that the core has phi^(-d) of the inradius of the hull for d = 2, 3, 4, and carry the dissection out for the first time on the 120-cell. The foundation is the arithmetic of the golden ring Z[phi], the ring of integers of Q(sqrt 5): vertices and hyperplanes live in Z[phi]^d, every orientation test is the exact sign of an element of Z[phi], decided with integers, and the pieces are named by sign vectors. We develop this foundation from scratch (conjugation, norm, units, the primes sqrt 5, 2, 3, the exact sign test, the lattice x -> (x, conj x), the vertex modules of the dodecahedron and the 120-cell, the icosian ring) and let it carry the geometry. The definition bifurcates in dimension four: the star cut at depth phi^(-4), a unit, has 2,455,201 cells in 338 orbits of H4; the hereditary cut at depth 1 - phi^(-4) = sqrt 5 / phi^2, a unit times the ramified prime, induces the three-dimensional dissection on every facet and has 8,161 cells in 8 orbits. New here: all vertices of the dodecahedral and of the hereditary dissection lie in the vertex module of the polytope being cut, whereas the star cut needs the denominators 2, 3 and 5; the seven kinds of pieces of the dodecahedron are exactly the I_h-orbits of sign vectors, with stellation layer equal to the number of plus signs. We catalogue the four-dimensional pieces and treat the circumscribed disc, ball and 4-ball. Every number quoted is recomputed exactly by a script whose output is reproduced in an appendix.

papers.title: Moments of Magic Squares: Line-Sum Conditions, a Permutation Threshold, and Random Energies
papers.abstract: Every semi-magic square of order $n$ satisfies the axial moment identities $\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}j^m=\sum_{i,j}s_{ij}i^m=M(n)\sum_jj^m$ for all $m\ge1$, where $M(n)=n(n^2+1)/2$. For real matrices the converse requires $1\le m\le n-1$, whereas for arrangements of $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ fewer moments suffice once $n\ge14$. We define the permutation threshold $k^*(n)$ as the least $k$ such that every arrangement satisfying these identities for $1\le m\le k$ is semi-magic. In terms of the column-sum deviations $\gamma_j$, the degree-$k$ conditions state that $\sum_j\gamma_jt^j$ is divisible by $(t-1)^{k+1}$, linking $k^*(n)$ to the Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem. While Schur's bound on real zeros gives $k^*(n)\le\sqrt{2(n-1)\log(n^4/4)}$, we prove the converse realisability bound $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt2-o(1))\sqrt n$ (and $k^*(n)\ge(\sqrt6-o(1))\sqrt n$ when $4\mid n$) by perturbing semi-magic squares with complementary row pairs via horizontal swaps. We also show that $k^*(n)=n-1$ for $3\le n\le13$, $k^*(n)=n-2$ for $14\le n\le17$, and $k^*(n)\le n-3$ for $n\ge18$, and determine $k^*(n)$ for $18\le n\le40$ with computer assistance. Finally, at the $k=1$ level of the hierarchy, we specialise the Mantel--Hubert quadratic assignment variance formula to obtain exact means, variances, and limit laws under a uniform random arrangement for the full line-sum energy $E_{\mathrm{full}}$, for the four-term energy $E_4$ combining the first moments and the two diagonals, and for Loly's moment of inertia, and find that $|L_4|=14{,}639{,}440$ arrangements of order $4$ satisfy $E_4=0$.

papers.title: Strongly explicit Ramanujan 2-lift towers via Hilbert modular forms
papers.abstract: Expander graphs have been central objects of study for over fifty years. Ramanujan graphs attain the asymptotically optimal nontrivial adjacency-eigenvalue threshold for infinite fixed-degree families. The original arithmetic constructions by Lubotzky-Phillips-Sarnak (1988) and Margulis (1988), and the iterative $2$-lift method of Bilu-Linial (2006) provide different approaches to Ramanujan graph constructions. Motivated by work on Mealy automata, we combine both approaches to give the following new arithmetic construction. For every prime $p\equiv 1\pmod {17}$, we construct a infinite tower of $(p+1)$-regular non-bipartite Ramanujan graphs on $2^n$ vertices, with label-preserving $2$-lifts between consecutive levels. These construction is strongly explicit: for fixed $p$, a neighbor or lift sign is computable in $O_p(n^3)$ bit operations. The construction uses fixed algebraic $2$-adic transformations, specified by finite data computable in preprocessing depending only on $p$. The main number-theoretic tool is Blasius's Ramanujan-Petersson theorem for Hilbert modular forms, applied through the Jacquet-Langlands correspondence to obtain the sharp bound $|\lambda|\leq2\sqrt p$ for every nontrivial adjacency eigenvalue of our $(p+1)$-regular graphs. The transformations preserve $2$-adic distance, which gives the binary covers and an explicit formula for their signings.

papers.title: Fractional Iterates and Oscillatory Convergence
papers.abstract: The simple continued fractions for the Golden & Silver means are well-known. It is astonishing that, as far as we know, no one has published half-iterates (let alone quarter-iterates) for the corresponding algorithms. We also examine the cosine and logistic maps (with parameter $2 < \lambda < 3$).

papers.title: A Uniform Upper Bound on the Length of MDS Codes from Genus-Two Curves
papers.abstract: We study the maximal length of MDS algebraic geometry codes from genus-two curves over finite fields. Let $C_\mathcal{ L}(D,G)$ be such a code over $\mathbb F_q$, with length $n$ and dimension $k$. Assume that $3\leq k\leq n-3$. We prove that $n<(2q+10\sqrt q+16)/3$. This bound holds for every prime power $q$ and for both parities of $k$. It gives a uniform upper bound of $2q/3+O(\sqrt q)$ for the maximal length. The explicit bound is strictly smaller than $q+1$ when $q\geq125$.

papers.title: On the Complexity of Computing with p-adic Lattices
papers.abstract: We study the complexity of two fundamental problems attached to p-adic lattices: computing an N-orthogonal basis, and deciding whether a given basis is N-orthogonal. When the norm is supplied through an explicit diagonal representation, both problems are polynomial. However, in the black-box model, where the ultrametric norm N is fixed and only accessible through an evaluation oracle, we prove that both problems require $\Omega$(p^{v-1} ) queries in the worst case, where v $\le$ n is the largest multiplicity of a commensurability class of N and n is the dimension of the ambient vector space. We then analyse the optimality of these bounds by providing explicit algorithms. Our results answer formally an open question of Zhang, Deng and Wang and refine the recent results of Duan and Wu by providing pointwise query bounds depending on the norm's structure, in addition to uniform bounds.

papers.title: Special cycles and Picard groups of Baily--Borel compactifications
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer two basic questions concerning algebraic cycles on orthogonal Shimura varieties attached to lattices. First, we prove that Kudla's special cycles and Heegner cycles have the same rational span in every codimension. This fills a gap in the codimension-one argument of \cite[Remark 2.4]{BLMM17}, pointed out by Bruinier--Zuffetti \cite{BZ26}. Second, in dimension at least ten, we prove that the rational Picard group of the Baily--Borel compactification is generated by the Hodge class. The proof of the second result reduces, via isotropic induction on the discriminant form, to the K3-type case treated in our previous work.

papers.title: Class groups of polynomial Krull domains
papers.abstract: A polynomial Krull domain is a Krull domain contained between $\mathbb Z[X]$ and $\mathbb Q[X]$. The domains of this class are precisely the Noetherian integrally closed domains between these polynomial rings by a result of Heinzer, and they have been recently classified by Chang and the second author of this paper as rings of polynomials which are integer-valued over a finite set of ultrametric balls in $\mathbb C_p$, as $p$ ranges through the set of primes in $\mathbb Z$. We show here that every ideal class of a polynomial Krull domain contains a prime ideal. Furthermore, given such a Krull domain $R$, we prove that there exists a polynomial Krull domain $R'$ that is Dedekind, contains $R$ and has the same class group as $R$.

papers.title: On the Supersingular reduction of Cubic fourfolds with Complex Multiplication
papers.abstract: If $X$ is a K3 surface with complex multiplication by a CM field $E$, Kazuhiro Ito proved that the height of the reduction of $X$ in characteristic $p>0$, and its Artin invariant if it is supersingular, can be computed from the decomposition of $p$ in $E$. We present analogous results for cubic fourfolds by using the main theorem of complex multiplication for cubic fourfold, proved by Rikuto Ito.

papers.title: The Kodaira dimension and minimal models of $\mathcal{A}_6$
papers.abstract: We prove that the moduli space $\mathcal{A}_6$ of principally polarized abelian sixfolds has Kodaira dimension zero, determining the remaining case in the Kodaira classification of the spaces $\mathcal{A}_g$. More precisely, every nonzero scalar Siegel modular form of genus six, weight $k$ and positive boundary order $b$ satisfies $k\geq 7b$, with equality precisely for powers of the weight-fourteen harmonic theta series of Dittmann, Salvati Manni and Scheithauer. The canonical ring is therefore a polynomial ring on one generator of degree two. We also prove numerical dimension zero and construct the unique projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial terminal minimal model. Its Picard number is one and its canonical divisor has order two. The perfect cone compactification is a Mori dream space, and the birational automorphism group of $\mathcal{A}_6$ is trivial. The proof combines normal vanishing on the Prym locus, polar intersections on abelian boundary fibers, and an exact theta calculation. A discrepancy estimate recovers the modular open subset from the minimal model.

papers.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.

papers.title: Geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack
papers.abstract: The analytic Emerton-Gee stack is a rigid analytic moduli stack of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules over the Robba ring, and is expected to play a fundamental role in the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence for locally analytic representations. In this paper, we establish the fundamental geometric properties of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack: it is a rigid analytic Artin stack, normal, a local complete intersection, and equidimensional of the expected dimension. As an application, our normality result removes the reducedness hypothesis in the paper of Le, Strauch, and Wang, thereby yielding an unconditional proof of the conjecture on the global sections of the analytic Emerton-Gee stack formulated by Emerton, Gee, and Hellmann.

papers.title: The Borisov--Nuer conjecture and root decompositions in even unimodular Lorentzian lattices
papers.abstract: We prove that every vector of $\mathrm{II}_{8n+1,1}$, with $n\ge1$, is a sum of two roots if and only if $n=1$ or $2$. This settles the Borisov--Nuer conjecture and implies the existence of Ulrich line bundles for every very ample polarization on a complex unnodal Enriques surface. For vectors of negative norm, we express the number of root decompositions as a Fourier coefficient of a vector-valued theta series, reducing existence to positivity. The main analytic difficulty is to obtain estimates uniform over lattices of unbounded determinant. We address this by combining a reduction based on primitive sublattices of codimension one and least determinant with explicit bounds for theta norms and Fourier coefficients of cusp forms.

papers.title: Diamonds: Homology and the Central Series of Groups
papers.abstract: We establish an analog of a theorem of Stallings which asserts the homomorphisms between the universal nilpotent quotients induced by a homomorphism $G \to H$ of groups are isomorphisms provided a pair of homological conditions are satisfied. Our analogy does not have a homomorphism between $G$ and $H$ but instead $G,H \leq G_0$ that satisfies a similar homological condition. We derive a few applications of this result. First, we show that there exist pairs of non-isomorphic number fields whose absolute Galois groups have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. We show that there exists pairs of non-isometric hyperbolic $n$-manifolds whose fundamental groups are residually nilpotent and have isomorphic universal nilpotent quotients. These are the first examples of residually nilpotent Kleinian groups with arbitrarily large nilpotent genus. Complex hyperbolic 2-manifold examples are given as well. Considering Riemann surfaces and complex hyperbolic 2-manifolds as projective curves and surfaces defined over a number field, we show the (outer) action of the absolute Galois group of the field of definition on the universal nilpotent quotients of the geometric fundamental groups are equivalent. This is in contrast to fact that the (outer) Galois action on the geometric fundamental group of a projective hyperbolic curve determines the curve by work of Mochizuki. In particular, the nilpotent representation theory of the geometric fundamental group is not anabelian.

papers.title: Approximation of adelic divisors and equidistribution of small points
papers.abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the Galois orbits of generic sequences of algebraic points of small height in a projective variety over a number field. Our main result is a generalization of Yuan's equidistribution theorem that applies to heights for which Zhang's lower bound for the essential minimum is not necessarily an equality. It extends to all projective varieties a theorem of Burgos Gil, Philippon, Rivera-Letelier and the second author for toric varieties. It also applies to sums of canonical heights for an algebraic dynamical system, and in particular it recovers K\"uhne's semiabelian equidistribution theorem. We also generalize previous work of Chambert-Loir and Thuillier to obtain new logarithmic equidistribution results. Finally we extend our main result to the quasi-projective setting recently introduced by Yuan and Zhang.

papers.title: Rank-Two Drinfeld Modules over Elliptic Coordinate Rings
papers.abstract: Let ${\mathbf A}$ be the affine coordinate ring of $E\setminus\{\infty\}$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $\mathbb F_q$ and $\infty$ is rational. We solve the rank-two case of the open problem of explicitly classifying sign-normalized Drinfeld ${\mathbf A}$-modules in generic characteristic with a fixed determinant motive; the classification for rank greater than two remains open. Outside an explicit exceptional locus, the rank-two Drinfeld modules are parametrized by the open modular curve $Y^{q+1}=\pi(X)$ with $Y\neq0$. The polynomial $\pi$ is squarefree, and the smooth projective completion of this curve has genus $q^2$. The roots of $\pi$ split into two types. Above roots of the first type, all coefficient functions extend regularly, and their extensions yield exactly the exceptional modules. Roots of the second type correspond to cusps of the modular curve; above these roots, the coefficient family has poles.

papers.title: Bad Reduction of Genus Two Curves with complex multiplication
papers.abstract: We study genus two curves whose Jacobians have complex multiplication by a biquadratic CM field. In this setting the Jacobian decomposes as a product of two elliptic curves with complex multiplication by orders in the same imaginary quadratic field. We derive upper bounds for the primes of stable bad reduction of such curves in terms of the discriminants of the CM orders. To do so, we give an explicit description of principally polarized abelian surfaces with CM by a biquadratic field via small CM cycles on an orthogonal Shimura variety of signature (3,2). We use it to prove an arithmetic intersection formula between such CM cycles with Humbert surfaces in terms of coefficients of incoherent Eisenstein series and representation numbers of ternary positive definite quadratic forms. Finally, employing the arithmetic properties of higher Green functions, we show that primes of stable bad reduction always exist.

papers.title: A logarithmic error term for subset sums of zero-sum-free sets
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $k$, let $f(k)$ be the minimum number of distinct nonempty subset sums of a zero-sum-free $k$-element set, where the minimum is taken over all finite abelian groups. We prove $f(k)\ge \frac{k^2}{2}-13k\log(k+1)-116k$. Together with the classical upper bound, this gives $f(k)=k^2/2+O(k\log k)$, with the optimal leading coefficient. As a consequence, the Olson constant of every finite abelian group $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{Ol}(G)\le\sqrt{2|G|}+O(\log|G|)$. The argument combines a triangular lower bound for repeated supports, a count using blocks of two and three copies, and a greedy expansion argument. No restriction is imposed on the order of the group or on the stabilizer of the set of subset sums.

papers.title: Davenport constants with growing binary rank
papers.abstract: We study the correction to the standard lower bound $D^*$ for Davenport constants of finite abelian groups with a growing elementary two-component. For every fixed nontrivial abelian $p$-group $H$ of odd order, we prove $D(H\oplus C_2^r)=D^*(H\oplus C_2^r)+(D(H)-1)\log_2 r+O_H(1)$, with a uniform version for varying $H$. For $C_3\oplus C_2^r$, we determine exact values on explicit infinite intervals of ranks. More generally, the correction is logarithmic or smaller precisely when the fixed group has at most one odd prime divisor. We show that the two-primary part affects the logarithmic coefficient: for $C_{24}\oplus C_2^r$, the ratio $(D-D^*)/\log_2 r$ has limsup at least $2.4933231\ldots>2$, whereas for $C_3\oplus C_2^r$ the limit is $2$. These upper limiting coefficients are unbounded even with the odd prime fixed. The proofs use binary codes and finite-field Fourier analysis.

papers.title: Arithmetic classification of the Dirichlet eigenvalues for a one-dimensional nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problem
papers.abstract: We classify the arithmetic nature of the Dirichlet eigenvalues of a homogeneous nonlocal one-dimensional $p$-Laplacian problem with power-type nonlinearity $|u|^{q-2}u$. For rational $p,q>1$, either all eigenvalues are algebraic or all are transcendental. Algebraicity holds exactly when the interval length is an algebraic multiple of a distinguished scale determined by a beta value. This scale is transcendental. When $p=q$, the criterion reduces to algebraicity of the interval length divided by $\pi$,independently of the rational exponent.

papers.title: Solutions to several problems on infinite sumset configurations
papers.abstract: We resolve a number of the problems collected by Kra, Moreira, Richter and Robertson in their survey "Problems on infinite sumset configurations in the integers and beyond". Our main result is that in every countably infinite abelian group, every set of positive upper Banach density contains a sumset $B_1+\dots+B_k$ of $k$ infinite sets, for every $k$; the proof uses the Kronecker factor, but no higher-order Host-Kra structure theory, nilsystems of step greater than one, or nilspaces. We also answer, positively or negatively, questions on monochromatic sets $B+mB$, on sumsets in sets of logarithmic density, on polynomial sumset configurations, on sums of the form $B_{i_1}+\dots+B_{i_m}$ with $B_i$ drawn from a density family, on random sets, on ordered sumsets in shifted primes, on sums and products in $\mathbb{N}$ and $\mathbb{Q}$, and on sumsets in abelian groups. Several of these answers concern the questions as literally stated, and two follow directly from known examples; in each case we say so and discuss the natural corrected question. Finally, answering a question of Kousek and Radi\'c, we show that the supremum of the lower Banach densities of sets $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B+t\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and every $t\ge0$ (respectively $B+B\not\subset A$ for every infinite $B$) is $1/2$ (respectively $3/4$). The main theorem and most of the other results are formalized in Lean 4, with some published theorems entering as explicit hypotheses.

papers.title: The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
papers.abstract: After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the P\'olya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the P\'olya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.

papers.title: Non-Archimedean Rigidity and the Uniform Dynamical Manin--Mumford for $\left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$
papers.abstract: We prove a uniform form of the dynamical Manin-Mumford conjecture for split endomorphisms $\Phi = \left(f_1,\ldots,f_n\right): \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n \to \left(\mathbb{P}^1\right)^n$ over $\mathbb{C}$, where each $f_i$ has degree $d \geq 2$ and at most one $f_i$ is exceptional. Specifically, we bound the number of irreducible components of $\overline{\operatorname{Prep}\left(\Phi\right)\cap V\left(\mathbb{C}\right)}^{\operatorname{Zar}}$ uniformly, depending only on $\left(n,d,\operatorname{deg} V\right)$. We also obtain uniform statements for the dynamical Bogomolov conjecture. Our approach combines a degeneration argument via ultrafilters with a new non-archimedean rigidity theorem, along with the quantitative dynamical Zhang's inequality by Mavraki and the second author.

papers.title: A p-adic Valuation Calculus for Permutations with Restricted Cycle Lengths
papers.abstract: Let a_A(n) be the number of permutations of {1,...,n} all of whose cycle lengths lie in a set A. We develop a valuation calculus for these numbers. Mobius inversion writes the exponential generating function as an Euler product, and at a prime p the factors with non-p-integral exponents, the blocks, determine a finite knapsack problem. Its optimal value gives a lower bound for v_p(a_A(n)), and the bound is attained exactly when one residue modulo p, the sum of the terms of the optimal choices, does not vanish. For a fixed set A and prime p the bounds and residues for all n <= N cost O(N^2) operations. When one block is strictly the most efficient, the valuation inside each residue class is that of a locally analytic p-adic function. We use the calculus to determine the 2-adic and 3-adic valuations for cycle lengths at most 3, 4 and 5, to prove the divisibility conjectures recorded in A378495, A079128, A193437 and A193438 and the 3-adic statements recorded in A057693 and A070945, and to treat 99 OEIS sequences in all. We also prove sharp divisibility and gcd theorems, show that at n = 111 the gcd of the counts over all sets of excluded cycle lengths containing {1,2,3} is one third of the gcd over the sets {1,2,3,k}, and determine eventual divisibility and tail gcds modulo composite integers. Part of the paper is formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: Arithmetic Poisson summation formulas
papers.abstract: We formulate Poisson summation with periodic weights in forms adapted to arithmetic sums (arithmetic Poisson summation formulas, APSF), in scalar, polynomial-congruence and vector-divisibility versions, extending Berndt's arithmetic Poisson formula. We use APSF as a common framework to rederive Ramanujan's formula for $\zeta(2m+1)$ and its character analogues due to Katayama and Berndt-Straub, the functional equations of $\zeta$, of Dirichlet's beta function and of Estermann's function, and the exponents of Tolev and Chen-Wang for power-free values of $x^2+y^2+1$ and $x^2+y^2+z^2+k$. It also gives reciprocity laws with Kelvin-function kernels for Lambert series twisted by a Dirichlet character over imaginary quadratic fields of arbitrary class number; asymptotic formulas with error terms for $r$-free values of $x_1^2+\cdots+x_n^2+k$, with Gaussian-weighted versions and the meromorphic continuation of the associated Dirichlet series; an argument of Terras, relating two-dimensional Bessel series for all odd zeta values and even Dirichlet beta values; and a Gaussian representation of a Mersenne-Fermat prime detector.

papers.title: The View-Obstruction Problem for Spheres in Dimensions Six and Seven
papers.abstract: Place closed Euclidean balls of radius r at the points of (1/2, 1/2, ..., 1/2) + Z^n. The view-obstruction problem for spheres asks for the least r such that every ray from the origin into the open positive orthant meets a ball. Equivalently, it asks for D_n = sup_v min_{t in R} sum_i ||t v_i - 1/2||{Z}^2 over positive integer vectors v, where ||x||{Z} denotes the distance from x to the nearest integer. The values for n <= 5 are classical. We prove D_6 = 107/312, attained only by permutations of (12, 9, 7, 5, 3, 2), and D_7 = 73/180, attained only by permutations of (11, 10, 8, 7, 4, 3, 1). The proof reduces the supremum to a finite search. The key facts are an exact lower bound d_n(v) >= delta^2_U for every rational subspace U perpendicular to v, a matching fiber upper bound, and Banaszczyk's transference theorem, applied along the Korkine-Zolotarev flag of the dual lattice v^perpendicular intersection Z^n. The search is quotiented by signed coordinate permutations and carried out entirely in exact rational arithmetic. It terminates with a certificate: no node of the search is left unresolved, and every surviving candidate is evaluated exactly. The method also recovers the known values for n = 3, 4, 5.

papers.title: CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
papers.abstract: Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds. To investigate the next term, we compare the normalized Robin difference with Ramanujan's oscillatory expression involving the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. The resulting difference has a slowly varying component on both CA and CA2. Its scaled values continue to vary over the computed range, leading to questions about convergence, upper bounds, and higher-order terms. We describe the sampling used in the figures and estimate the error from truncating the sum over zeros.

papers.title: Rational points of exact period three for the quadratic family
papers.abstract: For the quadratic family $f_c(x) = x^2 + c$ over $\Q$, we isolate a general $S$-unit and ABC template for rational periodic cycles: under the ABC conjecture, any rational quantity built from the consecutive-point sums of a rational period-$n$ cycle whose value and shift-by-$1$ are both $S$-units (with $S$ the support of the denominator of $c$) has logarithmic height at most $(1+\eps)\sum_{p \in S} \log p + O_\eps(1)$. Specializing to period $3$ in the change of coordinates $u = x_0 + x_1$ and $v = x_0 + x_2$, the period-$3$ condition reduces to $v = -1/(1+u)$, forcing the parameter $t = u$ to satisfy $t, t+1 \in \Z[S^{-1}]^\times$; the template then yields, under ABC, $\max\{|a|,|b|,|a+b|\} \le C_\eps \rad(d)^{1+\eps}$ for $t = a/b$ in lowest terms. We also characterize the period-$3$ locus on the $(u,v)$-plane intrinsically, isolating the ghost curve. Extending the height bound to higher periods remains an open structural question.

papers.title: Isospectral congruence manifolds, spectral rigidity, and a converse to Vign\'eras
papers.abstract: Let $B$ be a quaternion division algebra over a number field $k$ that gives rise to arithmetic Fuchsian or Kleinian groups, and let $\mathcal{O}$ be a maximal order of $B$. We show that every closed orientable Riemannian manifold isospectral to a principal congruence hyperbolic surface $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is isometric to $X_{\mathcal{O}'}(\mathfrak{a})$ for some maximal order $\mathcal{O}'$ of $B$, provided that no prime factor of $\mathfrak{a}$ ramifies in $B$ and that $\mathfrak{a}$ satisfies a mild condition at the primes over $2$. This is a converse to the construction of Vign\'eras, which produces isospectral manifolds from maximal orders of different types. In particular the spectral genus of $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ has at most $t(B)$ elements, and $X_\mathcal{O}(\mathfrak{a})$ is spectrally rigid when the type number $t(B)$ is one. In dimension three we prove the same statements for manifolds that, in addition, have the same complex lengths of closed geodesics. The proof rests on a local result that characterizes, by traces alone, the subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}(2)$ over a $p$-adic ring that are conjugate into a principal congruence subgroup by traces. As applications, every principal congruence Hurwitz surface is spectrally rigid, among them Klein's quartic, the Fricke-Macbeath surface and the surfaces of the first Hurwitz triplet, which partially answers a question of Reid.
